name: Ezra Apple
headline: Software Engineer | AI Products & Agent Systems

education.degree: B.S. in Electrical Engineering and Computer Science

highlights: Owned reusable-content workflows for Replo’s AI e-commerce platform, from service APIs and authentication through editor integration and live previews. Built the Component Library and template installation to let merchants reuse React storefront components across pages, contributing to the team’s beta-to-GA launch.
Designed and ran agent evaluations using customer-derived and synthetic editing tasks, comparing context and instruction changes on edit-target correctness, cost, and latency.

Redesigned persistent agent memory with scoped user/project context, compact working indexes, and automatically curated topic pages retrieved on demand; shipped a memory browser for inspecting saved context.
Hardened cloud-sandbox editing and live previews against stale builds and styles, adding runtime checks, bounded automatic recovery, actionable diagnostics, and preview restart controls.

Led consolidation of Replo’s agent skills and development workflows, organizing engineering, design, and support guidance; reduced the agent-facing catalog from 75 to 42 skills and added authoring standards, CI checks, and routing tests across Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and opencode.
Co-founded AI video translation startup, accepted into UC Berkeley SkyDeck Pad-13 incubator program.

Architected an asynchronous media-processing pipeline on AWS (S3, Lambda, Step Functions, SES) with fault-tolerant retries for long-running translation jobs and user-visible processing and failure states.
Owned an end-to-end video-translation MVP combining ElevenLabs dubbing with lip-sync, spanning authentication, media upload, processing orchestration, and launch site.
Ran a closed beta with 10+ content creators, using their feedback to refine the product and go-to-market.
Applied random forests and Bayesian optimization to ion-source diagnostic data, modeling accelerator performance and exploring configurations to maximize ion output.
Presented findings to senior researchers supporting heavy-element synthesis, including the element 120 program.

projects.name: ShoutOut
highlights: Built and shipped a local-first macOS dictation app in Swift that inserts transcribed speech into other apps, with signed, notarized releases and automatic updates.
Fine-tuned BERT Mini as a KEEP/DELETE token classifier for dictation cleanup, then exported it to Core ML and integrated on-device inference into the app’s transcription pipeline.
Streamed microphone PCM to a local Parakeet/Metal transcription helper with session-based capture, final decoding on completion, and a local full-clip fallback.
